title: Trust the date on the notice.

pages.title: The law said today. The customs office said January.
The law said today. The customs office said January., continued

the-law-said-today-the-customs-office-sa.title: The law said today. The customs office said January.
the-law-said-today-the-customs-office-sa.dek: Germany's tobacco tax law came into force on Wednesday by mistake, more than two months early on paper. Within hours the customs administration had published what still applies, and the finance ministry had started a correction. The error is embarrassing; the repair is the part worth watching.
the-law-said-today-the-customs-office-sa.text: On Tuesday the federal law raising Germany’s tobacco tax was published in the Federal Law Gazette. It sets out steps up in the tax for 2027 to 2030 [1]. Its final clause reads: “This law enters into force on the day after its promulgation” [2]. That day was Wednesday, 21 October 2026 [1]. Read literally, the higher rates applied from this morning, more than two months before anyone intended. The finance ministry confirmed the error on Wednesday. Bild had reported it first [2]. A spokesman called it a technical mistake in the date of entry into force [2]. At the government press conference, the ministry added a detail that matters more than the apology: the error was already in its own draft bill, and it was not caught anywhere in the procedure, in government or in parliament [2][3]. Asked how many people had read the text, the ministry said the number of hands and eyes could not be counted on two hands [3]. What the machinery did next. The striking thing is not the slip. Long laws carry slips. It is the order in which the repair arrived. On the day of publication, the customs administration, which collects the tax, put a notice on its website. It called the clause an “obvious inaccuracy” and stated plainly what applies [1]. The rates in force on 19 October continue unchanged until 31 December 2026 [1]. The new tariff for cigarettes, fine-cut, heated tobacco and substitutes starts on 1 January 2027, and for cigars, cigarillos, pipe and water-pipe tobacco on 1 March 2027 [1]. The notice also explains why the law entered into force early at all: so that the new tax stamps can be designed and ordered in time [1]. That is a small document doing a large job. Anyone at a tobacco wholesaler, a kiosk or a tax office who wanted to know what to do on Wednesday morning did not need a minister. They needed a dated notice from the authority that sends the bills, and it was there. The legal argument. At the press conference the finance ministry said the will of the legislator was clear from the law itself [3]. The explanatory memorandum names 1 January 2027 in 13 places, the ministry said, and the amended section 2 of the tobacco tax law begins each time with “for the period from 1 January 2027” [3]. The ministry said it is aiming to use the correction procedure under §61 of the joint rules of procedure of the federal ministries, so that the Bundestag does not have to vote again, because the error is obvious [3]. It also said it was working on instructing the administration not to collect the higher rates [3]. Details were not yet settled on Wednesday [3]. Asked who was responsible, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius pointed to the ministry that drafts the text; the chancellery coordinates, he said, and the federal president checks constitutionality [3]. The industry’s view. The tobacco makers were relieved and cross. Maximilian van Ackeren of the VdR, a tobacco industry association, called it “dilettantism” [2]. Jan Mücke of the BVTE, another industry association, warned that the sector would spend weeks “in a grey zone” tolerated by the authorities and asked for legal certainty quickly [2]. Both points are fair. Tolerance is not the same as law, and a correction that takes weeks would leave honest firms technically on the wrong side of a statute. What is actually at stake. Tagesschau notes that the reform could raise the price of a pack of 20 cigarettes by about four euros to €11.78 by 2030 [2]. The tax is expected to bring in about €1.5 billion extra next year, against €17.6 billion collected in 2025 [2]. None of that changes because of the slip. What changes is a few weeks of paperwork. A second correction, same room. The same press conference produced a quieter repair. This desk reported this morning that the “more than €220 billion” announced at Tuesday’s investment summit was a total for the year, not a summit haul. On Wednesday the economy ministry gave the exact figure, €228.6 billion. It covers large investment projects of €100 million or more announced by companies during 2026 [3]. Some were announced at the summit, but not all, and the ministry said it has no figure for the share that is new [3]. That is less impressive than the headline, and more useful: you now know the method. The argument. Two numbers were wrong or loose on Tuesday, and both were made precise on Wednesday, on the record, in answer to plain questions. That is how institutions are supposed to work. A free press asks; a ministry answers; an agency publishes a notice that a shopkeeper can read. You will hear more today about embarrassment. The better story is the speed of the repair. Watch whether the correction is formally published, and how soon. That will be the receipt.

nine-ships-and-a-fire-off-bukha.title: Nine ships and a fire off Bukha
nine-ships-and-a-fire-off-bukha.dek: A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile near the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday morning, and by mid-afternoon an open ship-tracking counter had logged nine commercial crossings for the day. Both facts are true, and neither is the whole picture.
nine-ships-and-a-fire-off-bukha.text: On Wednesday a tanker was struck by “an unknown projectile” about 11 nautical miles off Bukha, on Oman’s side of the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said [1]. A fire broke out and the ship is “now at anchor” [1]. “All crew are reported as safe. There is no reported environmental impact at this time,” UKMTO said [1]. TradeWinds, the shipping paper, says fresh incidents have pushed the confirmed tally of Iranian attacks beyond 30 vessels in three weeks [3]. AFP notes that attacks have increased as Washington escorts more ships through the strait [1]. The counter. Hormuz.now, a site that counts commercial crossings from ships’ public AIS signals, had logged nine crossings by 14:26 UTC on Wednesday: five into the Gulf and four out, one of them a small products tanker [2]. Its rolling seven-day average is 2.3 crossings a day, against a pre-crisis baseline of 84.8 [2]. The ships it saw today were mostly bulk carriers and general cargo, bound for ports such as Jebel Ali, Sohar and Umm Qasr [2]. Read the method before the number. The site is candid about what it misses. Its counts are “AIS-visible only and miss ships running dark”, and it excludes small craft; six of those crossed by the same hour [2]. A ship that switches off its transponder to avoid being targeted does not appear. So the counter is a floor, not a total. The official comparison, IMF PortWatch, publishes several days late; its latest day is 18 October [2]. Why this matters to you. Fuel and freight prices in Europe still lean on this water. A floor of nine visible ships tells you the route is not working normally; it does not tell you it is closed. A fire tells you the risk is real; it does not tell you traffic has stopped. When two careful sources disagree, the gap is usually method, not malice. The constructive habit is the same as this morning: take the count with its footnote. The day the visible number rises for a week in a row, without fires, that will be the news.

lingen-and-the-fuel-rods-for-the-east.title: Lingen, Rosatom and the fuel rods for the east
lingen-and-the-fuel-rods-for-the-east.dek: Lower Saxony has allowed Rosatom into the fuel-element plant at Lingen. Berlin says the plant helps eastern Europe away from Russian supply, and that there is no EU majority to sanction such cases.
lingen-and-the-fuel-rods-for-the-east.text: At Wednesday’s government press conference in Berlin, ZDF asked how warnings about Russian sabotage fit with a permission for Rosatom, Russia’s state nuclear company, to take part in the fuel-element factory at Lingen [1]. The question followed a statement by Lower Saxony’s environment ministry that the approval had been given [1]. The federal environment ministry said the decision was taken by the Land ministry. The plant is run within a multinational web of companies with links to a Russian firm, it said, and EU law permits manufacturing material for nuclear power supply as a business [1]. The security situation is reassessed regularly; the business activity is not in itself an automatic threat [1]. Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius added the economic logic. Fuel elements of this type made in Lingen mainly supply power plants in eastern Europe, he said, which could become more independent of deliveries from Russia [1]. The permission was granted by Lower Saxony in consultation with Berlin [1]. The federal government wants the sanctions regime extended to cases like this, Kornelius said, but there is no majority for that in the EU [1]. So the dull question is not who is in the boardroom. It is whose reactors stop needing Russian rods, and when.

a-directive-is-not-a-plan.title: A directive is not a plan
a-directive-is-not-a-plan.dek: On Wednesday evening Israel's prime minister told cadets he had ordered the Iranian regime toppled. On the same day Tehran said the negotiating table was still in place. Only one of those comes with paperwork.
a-directive-is-not-a-plan.text: Speaking at an officer graduation ceremony in the Negev on Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu said he had directed the Israeli army, the Mossad and the security services to topple the government in Tehran [1]. “There is only one way to remove this threat once and for all,” he said [1]. CBS News notes that he did not say how [1]. The same report carries the other side of the day. Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said indirect talks with Washington over a seven-day ceasefire proposal were continuing through mediators including Pakistan and Qatar, and that the US wanted to add clauses [1]. “The negotiating table remains in place,” he said [1]. Citing the Financial Times, CBS also reports that President Trump blocked a planned multi-day Israeli strike operation for the weekend of 10 October [1]. And Egypt’s president said Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory” and did not include an attack on Yemen [1]. A sentence at a graduation is a speech. A mediator’s flight schedule, a clause under negotiation and a strike that was called off are the machinery. Tonight the machinery is still running, slowly, and that is the part to watch. Nothing here is advice.

berlin-rejects-the-libya-turkey-sea-line.title: Berlin rejects the Libya–Turkey sea line
berlin-rejects-the-libya-turkey-sea-line.dek: After Libya's House of Representatives approved a maritime memorandum with Turkey, the German foreign office said it rejects it and points to EU Council conclusions from 2019.
berlin-rejects-the-libya-turkey-sea-line.text: Libya’s House of Representatives has approved the memorandum with Turkey that draws maritime zones in the eastern Mediterranean, a Greek reporter noted at Berlin’s government press conference [1]. The foreign office said it had taken note and agreed with the EU Commission and Council presidents [1]. Turkey and Libya must respect EU members’ sovereign rights, and sea boundaries must follow international law and involve all coastal states, it said [1]. Asked about sanctions, the spokeswoman said that was getting ahead of things; Berlin rejects the memorandum and will discuss next steps in the EU [1]. Sea lines matter because gas fields follow them.

europe-was-sorted-by-receipts-not-moods.title: Europe was sorted by receipts, not moods
europe-was-sorted-by-receipts-not-moods.dek: A Ray-Ban maker jumped about 15% and a supermarket chain fell about 14% on the same Wednesday morning. Both moves came from quarterly figures, and one of them priced the French curfews into a forecast.
europe-was-sorted-by-receipts-not-moods.text: By early afternoon on Wednesday the pan-European STOXX 600 was up 0.7%, after a session on Tuesday in which it fell as much as 1% before ending virtually flat [1]. Germany’s DAX was up 1% and France’s CAC 40 0.8%; London’s FTSE 100 was largely flat after UK inflation rose more than expected to 3.5% [1]. Index levels are the least interesting part of the day. The spread between individual shares told you more. The top of the list. EssilorLuxottica, which makes Ray-Ban glasses, rose more than 15% after third-quarter revenue beat expectations [1]. Adidas gained 2.5% after raising its full-year outlook [1]. European chip-equipment makers BE Semiconductor, ASM International and ASML, and the chipmaker STMicroelectronics, each rose more than 2% [1]. The bottom. Carrefour fell nearly 14% after cutting its annual forecast and saying that riots, looting and curfews had raised costs and disrupted trading [1]. That is the French unrest arriving where it eventually has to: in a company’s guidance, written in euros. A curfew is a public order measure. For a retailer it is also shorter opening hours, extra security and damaged stock. The expectations bar. Analysts polled by Reuters expect third-quarter earnings at STOXX 600 companies to grow 20.7% from a year earlier, slower than the 24.0% of the second quarter but still fast [1]. More than half of the index by market value reports over the next two weeks [1]. A high bar makes results matter more, in both directions, as Wednesday showed. Across the Atlantic. Wall Street opened higher: the Dow up 0.30% at 52,652.85, the S&P 500 up 0.31% at 7,736.43 and the Nasdaq up 0.67%, helped by results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer [2]. Netflix slipped after its forecast failed to impress [2]. Meta and Tesla report after the close [1]. Nothing here is advice; it is a reading of the day’s published figures.

jio-was-three-times-covered-by-teatime.title: Jio's order book was three times covered by teatime, and retail was not yet full
jio-was-three-times-covered-by-teatime.dek: India's largest IPO drew bids for 59.55 crore shares against 19.75 crore on offer on its first day. Institutions did nearly all of the work.
jio-was-three-times-covered-by-teatime.text: The initial public offering of Jio Platforms was subscribed 3.02 times by 5:24 pm Indian time on its first day, with bids for 59.55 crore shares against 19.75 crore on offer, according to BSE data reported by Moneycontrol [1]. (A crore is ten million.) The issue, India’s largest at about Rs 30,200 crore, has a price band of Rs 1,065 to 1,119 a share and closes on 23 October; listing is slated for 28 October [1]. The split matters more than the total. Qualified institutional buyers subscribed their portion 9.02 times; non-institutional investors 1.59 times; retail investors only 0.69 times [1]. Before the issue opened, Jio raised Rs 8,109.84 crore from 212 anchor investors, including BlackRock, Fidelity, GIC and Norway’s sovereign fund [1]. Grey-market trading implied a premium of about 22–23% over the top of the band on Wednesday morning [1]. That is an unofficial number from an unregulated market, and it is worth exactly what an unsigned quote is worth. The signed numbers are the order book, and they say the professionals came first. Nothing here is advice.

gold-fell-while-the-war-went-on.title: Gold fell for a fourth day while the war went on
gold-fell-while-the-war-went-on.dek: Bullion is about 26% below its January record. Expensive oil keeps rate rises in play, and an asset with no yield pays for that.
gold-fell-while-the-war-went-on.text: Spot gold slipped 0.2% to $4,118.18 an ounce early on Wednesday, its fourth daily fall, leaving it about 26% below its January record and about 22% lower since the war began [1]. The reason given is oil: expensive crude keeps inflation and further Federal Reserve rises in view, and gold pays no interest [1]. Futures put roughly a 16% chance on a Fed increase at the 27–28 October meeting [1]. A safe haven is only safe against the risk it was bought for.

the-unions-left-matignon-with-a-date.title: The unions left Matignon with a date, not a measure
the-unions-left-matignon-with-a-date.dek: France's prime minister met the main unions on Wednesday morning. The CGT says no measures were announced, and the unions confirmed a general strike call for 5 November.
the-unions-left-matignon-with-a-date.text: Sébastien Lecornu chaired a meeting at 10:30 on Wednesday with the main French unions, the CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA and FSU [1]. The ministers for public accounts, labour, education and the interior attended, together with the heads of the national police, the gendarmerie and the Paris police prefecture [1]. Leaving Matignon, CGT leader Sophie Binet said the government had “announced no measure” and had not taken the unions’ demands into account [1]. She relayed the joint union call for a general strike on 5 November [1]. Two other dates are now on the calendar. Education minister Édouard Geffray told the National Assembly that a “first series of decisions” would be presented to schools, regions and pupils on Monday morning [1]. In the Senate, Lecornu said he was “lucid” about the “climate of social tension and anxiety” and refused “announcement effects” [1]. Speaking from Doha, President Emmanuel Macron said a state of emergency was not needed [1]. The useful reading: a meeting with no measures is not a failure if it produces a timetable. Monday’s education decisions are the first thing you can actually check.

flood-cover-by-default-not-by-decree.title: Flood cover by default, not by decree
flood-cover-by-default-not-by-decree.dek: Berlin's justice and finance ministries published a discussion paper on Wednesday: new home insurance policies would come with natural-hazard cover built in.
flood-cover-by-default-not-by-decree.text: Germany’s justice and finance ministries published a joint discussion paper on insurance against natural hazards on Wednesday [1]. The proposal: new residential building policies would only be offered with cover for floods and other natural hazards, and existing policies would be switched over on a fixed date [1]. The justice ministry said 98% of residential buildings already have building insurance, so extending those policies would cover most homes [1]. Different deductibles may be offered [1]. Länder and associations will now be consulted [1]. It is a default, not a mandate; defaults tend to work.

the-nurse-lost-and-the-patients-improved.title: The nurse lost the test, and the patients still got better
the-nurse-lost-and-the-patients-improved.dek: A Stockholm trial pitted a few nurse visits against guided self-help therapy for stress. The therapy did better, the nurses failed the statistical bar they were set, and both groups were markedly less stressed a year later.
the-nurse-lost-and-the-patients-improved.text: Researchers at Karolinska Institutet randomly assigned 172 primary-care patients in Stockholm with mild-to-moderate stress-related ill health to one of two routes [1]. Eighty-five got nurse-led collaborative care: two to six visits over up to twelve weeks, built on problem-solving, explanation and care coordination [1]. Eighty-seven got guided self-help cognitive behavioural therapy: twelve weekly modules with support from a psychologist, online or as a book with sessions [1]. The study was published in BMJ Mental Health and summarised by Medscape on Wednesday [1]. The test the nurses failed. The question was whether the nurse route was “not worse” than the therapy by more than a set margin. It was not shown to be: the difference favoured the therapy (effect size 0.22), and the upper end of its confidence interval, 0.52, overshot the 0.3 margin [1]. That is a precise way of saying the trial cannot rule out that the nurses’ route is meaningfully weaker. The numbers both groups share. On the ten-item Perceived Stress Scale, the nurse group fell from 24.9 to 19.4 at twelve weeks and the therapy group from 25.8 to 18.4 [1]. A year later the scores were 16.3 and 15.2 [1]. Desk arithmetic: that is a drop of 8.6 points for the nurse route and 10.6 for the therapy, measured from where each group started. Patients in the nurse group needed on average 3.68 sessions [1]. What the study cannot say. There was no untreated group, so part of the improvement may be time itself [1]. It was one centre, and most participants were middle-aged, well-educated women [1]. Satisfaction ratings were similar in both arms [1]. The constructive reading. The authors’ own conclusion is modest: the nurse route is “safe, relatively easy to administer” and may still be useful in primary care [1]. That is the kind of finding that rarely makes a headline and often makes a service work. Not every patient needs the best-scoring option on day one; many need a competent first step that is available this month.

personality-moved-with-the-mood.title: Personality moved with the mood
personality-moved-with-the-mood.dek: In 334 inpatients at a German university hospital, neuroticism fell and extraversion rose as depression lifted. Whether that is change or a return to normal, the study cannot tell.
personality-moved-with-the-mood.text: Researchers from the University of Münster and Charité in Berlin followed 334 psychiatric inpatients who stayed at least four weeks, with questionnaires on admission, roughly every two weeks and just before discharge [1]. The work appeared in the Journal of Affective Disorders [1]. As depression scores fell, the patients described their personalities differently: neuroticism went down, conscientiousness and extraversion went up [1]. Those with higher average neuroticism improved more slowly on 14 of the 21 symptoms measured, from sadness to insomnia [1]. Higher extraversion went with faster relief on seven, including work difficulty, indecisiveness and pessimism [1]. The limits are stated plainly. The data are observational, treatments varied, and the personality test was a brief 15-item version with limited precision [1]. Above all, a depressed person tends to judge themselves harshly, so the shift may simply be a return to the patient’s usual self as the mood lifts [1]. That caveat is the useful part. A trait score taken on a bad week is a reading of the week as much as of the person. Clinicians who note it, and plan for a slower course where needed, are using the finding as intended.

happy-scenes-beat-your-own-goals.title: Happy scenes beat your own goals, briefly
happy-scenes-beat-your-own-goals.dek: A lab study found that imagining general good events raised the sense of control in students with more low-mood symptoms. Imagining their own goals did not.
happy-scenes-beat-your-own-goals.text: Psychologists at Hull and York St John gave 187 students one of four seven-minute tasks [1]. In those with more depressive symptoms, imagining positive future scenes raised their sense of control over their goals; only the general happy scenes kept the effect ten minutes later [1]. Imagining their own goal successes left some ratings lower after ten minutes [1]. One session, students not patients, not preregistered [1]. A small, honest result, and labelled as such.

podium-vs-print-cheap-power-has-not-reac.title: Podium vs Print: cheap power has not reached Germany's auction yet
podium-vs-print-cheap-power-has-not-reac.dek: An ECB blog published on Wednesday says renewables are pulling wholesale electricity prices down in many countries. Germany's day-ahead auction says October has so far cost about 80% more than the same days last year. Both are true, and the gap between them has a name: grids.
podium-vs-print-cheap-power-has-not-reac.text: The podium. On Wednesday three ECB economists published a long blog post on why the euro area has withstood this year’s energy shock better than feared [1]. One passage is about electricity. “The expansion of renewable generation capacity is reducing wholesale electricity prices in many countries,” they write, because more renewables mean fewer hours in which a gas plant sets the price [1]. The evidence they cite is specific. In Spain the share of hours in which gas set the price fell from around 80% in 2020 to just above 20% in the first nine months of 2026; in France it fell from around 60% to around 20% [1]. Unlike in 2021–22, they say, the latest shock hit countries with more renewable and nuclear power less hard [1]. The print. Germany’s day-ahead auction tells the other half. The daily average price for the Germany-Luxembourg zone was €169.93 per megawatt hour over 1 to 21 October 2026, against €94.14 for the same days of 2025 [2]. Desk arithmetic: that is about 80% higher. Wednesday’s delivery day cleared at €211.94 [2]. September averaged €144.82, with a high of €256.55 on 14 September [2]. The gap. The two are not contradicting each other as much as it looks. The blog does not name Germany, and its claim is about structure, measured over years [1]. The auction is about this autumn, in one bidding zone, on days when the wind and the sun decide how often gas is needed at the margin. The chart shows the shape plainly: through the spring and early summer, months after the shock began, German power mostly stayed between about €77 and €110; it was the autumn, with a second wave of higher gas prices, that lifted it [1][2]. Verdict. The podium is right about the direction, and the print is right about the bill. What closes the gap is in the same blog post: “further integration of EU electricity markets, including more cross-border interconnections and investment in grids”, so that cheaper renewable electricity “could flow where it is needed” [1]. That is dull machinery: cables, substations, permits. It is also the only part of the argument that turns a Spanish average into a German invoice. Nothing here is advice.

brent-rose-on-words-from-tehran.title: Brent rose $2 on words from Tehran and a count of attacked ships
brent-rose-on-words-from-tehran.dek: Iran's leaders said there was little reason to expect talks with Washington, and Kpler counted at least 18 vessel attacks in two weeks. Brent stood near $111 by midday in London.
brent-rose-on-words-from-tehran.text: Brent crude futures rose $2.06, or 1.9%, to $110.85 a barrel by 10:48 GMT on Wednesday, and US crude rose $2.13 to $99.95, Reuters reported [1]. On Tuesday Brent had touched its highest level in five months before falling back on talk of mediation between Iran and Pakistan [1]. Wednesday’s move came from words. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself, and President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the United States could not expect dialogue “while blockading and threatening Iran” [1]. The more durable information is in the shipping counts. Kpler data showed at least 18 vessel attacks over the past two weeks, and LSEG analysts said Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, into the Gulf of Oman [1]. On the other side of the ledger, industry figures from the American Petroleum Institute showed US crude stocks down 4.9 million barrels in the week to 16 October, with gasoline and distillates also lower [1]. Speeches move the price for an afternoon. Insurance premiums, tanker routes and inventories move it for a season. The official US inventory count from the Energy Information Administration follows the industry estimate; that is the one to wait for.

europes-gas-stores-stopped-filling.title: Europe's gas stores stopped filling at three-quarters
europes-gas-stores-stopped-filling.dek: EU storage is 74.6% full, about 16 points below the five-year norm for the date, and Germany is at 61%. Injection season is ending with the tanks short.
europes-gas-stores-stopped-filling.text: EU gas storage stood at 74.62% full on Wednesday, 15.9 percentage points below the five-year average of 90.5% for the date, according to GasRadar’s daily briefing [1]. The trend is flat, at about 0.01 points a day, as injection season winds down [1]. Poland is 98.7% full and Portugal 95.5%; Germany is at 61.2% and the Netherlands 64.7% [1]. The front-month Dutch TTF contract fell 3.38% to €85.06 per megawatt hour, the briefing said, after a rally from €73.51 on 5 October [1]. A storage figure is the dullest number in energy, and the one that decides how a cold February goes.

britain-printed-three-point-five-at-the-.title: Britain printed 3.5%, and most of it came through the pump
britain-printed-three-point-five-at-the-.dek: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September on motor fuels, while core prices moved less. The euro area showed the same split a week ago. Eight days before the ECB decides, the useful number is the second one.
britain-printed-three-point-five-at-the-.text: The Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday that consumer prices rose 3.5% in the 12 months to September, up from 3.1% in August and the highest rate since October 2025 [1]. Investing.com called it more than expected, and London’s FTSE 100 lagged the continent in the morning [3]. Where it came from. Transport made the largest upward contribution, “particularly motor fuels” [1]. Petrol averaged 169.5 pence a litre in September, up 8.2p in a month and the highest since August 2022; diesel averaged 192.5p, up 10.7p, the highest since July 2022 [1]. Motor fuel prices were 29.8% higher than a year earlier [1]. Heating oil (kerosene) rose 22.7% in the month [1]. Where it did not. Core inflation, which leaves out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, rose from 2.6% to 2.8% [1]. Food inflation stayed at 1.3%, the lowest since 2021 [1]. Services rose from 3.4% to 3.7%, partly on air fares, which fell less in September than a year earlier [1]. Desk arithmetic: the gap between headline and core is 0.7 percentage points. The same picture in Frankfurt’s data. The euro area showed the split more sharply. Headline HICP was 3.8% in September; core was 2.5% [2]. Desk arithmetic: a gap of 1.3 points. The ECB’s deposit rate is also 2.5%, after rises in June and September [2]. Lagarde told the IMF’s steering committee last week that wages have “so far shown no material response to the energy shock” [2]. What to take from it. A fuel shock shows up first in the headline and only later, if at all, in the core. The chart shows the deposit rate now level with core inflation, and the headline line well above both. That is the position the Governing Council takes into its meeting on 29 October. Britain’s print adds a second witness, not a new verdict. Nothing here is advice; it is a reading of published numbers.

britain-owes-three-trillion.title: Britain's debt passed £3 trillion, and the interest bill set a September record
britain-owes-three-trillion.dek: The ONS counted £24.5 billion of borrowing in September, £1.9 billion above forecast, a week before the Budget. A third of the interest bill was inflation uplift on index-linked gilts.
britain-owes-three-trillion.text: UK public sector net borrowing was £24.5 billion in September, £1.8 billion more than a year earlier and £1.9 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility’s forecast, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday [1]. It was the second-highest September on record, behind 2020 [1]. Public sector net debt was provisionally estimated at £3,005.0 billion at the end of September, above £3 trillion for the first time [1]. As a share of the economy it was 94.0% of GDP, 0.7 points lower than a year earlier, because nominal GDP grew faster than the debt [1]. The detail worth reading is the interest. Central government debt interest was £10.9 billion, the highest September since records began in 1997 [1]. Of that, £4.0 billion was the inflation uplift on index-linked gilts, largely from a 0.6% rise in the Retail Prices Index between June and July [1]. Desk arithmetic: that is a little over a third of the month’s interest bill. Inflation does not only reach households through the pump; it reaches the Treasury through the gilt register. For the financial year so far, borrowing was £97.8 billion, £4.4 billion less than a year earlier but £6.0 billion above forecast [1]. The Budget is on 28 October, with new OBR forecasts [1]. Nothing here is advice.

lane-wants-the-euro-to-carry-policy-abro.title: Lane made a monetary case for a global euro
lane-wants-the-euro-to-carry-policy-abro.dek: In Shanghai, the ECB's chief economist argued that wider use of the euro abroad would make its rate decisions bite harder, and import prices less jumpy.
lane-wants-the-euro-to-carry-policy-abro.text: Speaking in Shanghai on Wednesday, ECB chief economist Philip Lane said greater international use of the euro “supports the ability of the ECB to achieve price stability” by extending the reach of its policy to foreign demand [1]. More euro invoicing would also make euro-area import prices less sensitive to outside shocks, he said [1]. “The monetary-policy case for liquidity lines is reinforced by their dynamic interaction with other policy areas,” he added [1]. It is an argument for plumbing, made by an economist, which is the best kind.

ordinary-ledger-the-occasional-rider-wai.title: Ordinary Ledger: the occasional rider waits
ordinary-ledger-the-occasional-rider-wai.dek: This morning the Länder transport ministers were to discuss a monthly cap for people who ride the bus now and then. By the afternoon the motion had been taken off the agenda, on a majority vote, for arriving too late. The idea is not dead. It is unfiled.
ordinary-ledger-the-occasional-rider-wai.text: The proposal was called “Bundesweiter elektronischer Gelegenheitstarif”, a nationwide electronic tariff for occasional riders [1]. According to BR, citing people in the room, the Länder transport ministers took it off the agenda of their conference in Hohenschwangau on Wednesday by majority decision, because it had been submitted too close to the meeting [1]. What was on the table. North Rhine-Westphalia and Hamburg proposed a smartphone check-in, check-out fare: you register the start and end of each trip, the cheapest fare is worked out automatically, and in a month you never pay more than a Deutschlandticket [1][2]. That ticket costs €63 a month and rises to €66.80 in January [2]. Who said what. Bavaria’s transport minister Christian Bernreiter, who chairs the conference, had said before the session that there was certainly no money for it, with billions already missing, for example to order regional trains [1]. The association of German transport companies, the VDV, also rejected the idea [1]. Social welfare associations welcomed it as cheaper mobility for poorer people [1]. The ledger. Desk arithmetic: the January step is €3.80 a month, or €45.60 over a year for a full-year holder [2]. The proposed cap would have tied the occasional rider’s worst month to the same number. Tonight there is no such cap, and nothing has changed for anyone’s fare. The constructive reading. A procedural reason is the cheapest kind of no. It says nothing about the merits and invites a better-prepared motion. The ministers stay until Thursday, mostly on funding, with low water in German rivers and autonomous driving also on the programme [1]. If the money argument is serious, that is the room in which to put a euro figure next to it.

petrol-fell-diesel-did-not.title: Petrol fell, diesel did not
petrol-fell-diesel-did-not.dek: The ADAC's weekly comparison has E10 down 4.1 cents and diesel up 0.8 cents. Same oil, two directions, and the club names the reasons.
petrol-fell-diesel-did-not.text: A litre of Super E10 cost €2.110 on the national average on Wednesday, 4.1 cents less than a week earlier, according to the ADAC [1]. Diesel went the other way, up 0.8 cents to €2.255 [1]. The oil did not help either fuel. Brent reached its highest level since May during Tuesday’s trading and closed at about $109 a barrel, roughly $3 more than a week before [1]. For diesel, the ADAC adds a seasonal factor: demand for heating oil, a close cousin, rises as the weather turns colder [1]. Petrol’s fall despite dearer crude, the club argues, shows there was room for price cuts on E10, and it says most of the fuel-tax rebate now seems to be reaching the pump for petrol [1]. Desk arithmetic: diesel is now 14.5 cents a litre dearer than E10. On a 50-litre fill, E10 is €2.05 cheaper than a week ago and diesel €0.40 dearer. The ADAC’s standing observation is that prices are lowest shortly before 12:00 and jump at noon [1]. It is a pattern, not a promise. Nothing here is advice.

heating-oil-at-one-seventy-four.title: Heating oil at €1.74, and eight cents between Länder
heating-oil-at-one-seventy-four.dek: The national average rose about half a cent on Wednesday morning. Where you live mattered more than the day.
heating-oil-at-one-seventy-four.text: A litre of heating oil cost €1.74 on the German average on Wednesday morning, a good half cent more than on Tuesday, according to the trader HeizOel24 [1]. Hamburg was cheapest at €1.70 and Rhineland-Palatinate dearest at €1.78 [1]. Desk arithmetic: on a 3,000-litre delivery, that eight-cent gap is €240. Gasoil, the exchange price behind heating oil and diesel, was about $30 a tonne above Tuesday evening [1]. Austria averaged €1.83 [1]. Nothing here is advice.

a-data-centre-that-arrives-on-a-truck.title: A data centre that arrives on a truck
a-data-centre-that-arrives-on-a-truck.dek: Nvidia's new DSX Pod puts seven Vera Rubin racks, pre-cabled and liquid-cooled, into a container of about 28 tonnes. The claim is that a site can start serving in 14 days instead of six months. The bottleneck it attacks is not chips but building work.
a-data-centre-that-arrives-on-a-truck.text: At its GTC conference in Berlin on Wednesday, Nvidia announced the DSX Pod AI Factory: seven of its Vera Rubin AI racks packed into a unit roughly the size of a standard shipping container, weighing about 28,000 kilograms, and designed to travel by truck on normal roads [1]. The cabling and liquid cooling are assembled at the factory [1]. What is actually new. Not the chips. The change is where the work is done. “The only thing that has to happen when it gets to the site is it’s placed in its location, connected to the rest of the other containers, and validated through final burning and testing,” Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale computing, told reporters [1]. Nvidia says this cuts the time for a new AI data centre to start serving tokens from six months to 14 days [1]. That figure is the company’s own and is untested until the first pods arrive. Why Europe gets a mention. Nvidia said the pod is for customers worldwide and could help with deployment problems faced by European customers [1]. It did not spell out which. What the design does is move the cabling and cooling work from the site into a factory hall, where it can be done in series and checked before the unit leaves [1]. What it does not change. A pod still has to be placed, connected to the other containers and tested on site [1], and the site still needs its power connection; that does not come on the truck. Nvidia gave no price; analysts estimate a single Vera Rubin rack at more than $7 million [1]. Deliveries are expected from early 2027 through manufacturing partners including Foxconn, Gigabyte, Lenovo, HPE, Quanta and Pegatron [1]. The direction of travel. Nvidia has moved from selling single graphics chips to servers, then racks, and now containers of racks [1]. Jensen Huang said recently that what Nvidia sells into one gigawatt of data-centre capacity has gone from about $18 billion to “$40-plus billion per gigawatt” [1]. The investor question this week, as Meta and Tesla report, is whether buyers keep spending at that rate [2]. The engineering question is simpler and more useful: how much of a building can be made in a factory.

google-gave-away-the-npu-design.title: Google gave away the design, and Synaptics put it on a board you can buy
google-gave-away-the-npu-design.dek: The Coralboard SL developer kit, built on Google's open-source Coral NPU, is now on general sale. The faster SR200 chips are announced but still sampling, with no price.
google-gave-away-the-npu-design.text: Synaptics introduced its Astra SR200 series on 20 October, three AI microcontrollers rated at 200 to 400 GOPS and built around Google Research’s open-source Coral NPU design [1]. They are aimed at wearables, battery-powered sensors, connected cameras and industrial vision [1]. TechRepublic’s useful distinction is between what is announced and what is orderable. The SR200 chips remain in sampling, with no public price or firm production date [1]. What developers can buy now is a separate board, the Coralboard SL, which moved to full availability through DigiKey the same day and runs a 1-TOPS version of the Coral NPU on Synaptics’ existing SL2619 processor [1]. The licensing is the quieter story. Google released the Coral NPU architecture under the Apache 2.0 licence, so chipmakers can build it into their processors without royalties [1]. The pitch is that a model optimised once could run across chips from different vendors; TechRepublic notes that this remains a goal rather than something shown across competing commercial silicon [1]. Synaptics’ own speed figures for small language models have not yet been independently tested on shipping SR200 hardware [1]. A press release describes a chip. A distributor’s stock line describes a product. This week Synaptics has one of each.

nvidia-wants-agents-on-a-leash.title: Nvidia drew a fence around AI agents and listed who will use it
nvidia-wants-agents-on-a-leash.dek: The OpenShell reference architecture pairs agent software with hardware-level monitoring. The partner list is long; the proof will be in deployments.
nvidia-wants-agents-on-a-leash.text: At GTC Berlin on Wednesday, Nvidia announced the OpenShell Reference Architecture, a design for building, containing and monitoring AI agents on company infrastructure [1]. It combines its open-source OpenShell runtime with BlueField data-processing units running Nvidia’s Sentry software for “out-of-band monitoring of agent behavior and in-silicon policy enforcement” [1]. Nvidia names Anthropic, AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, SAP and Siemens among those working with it [1]. “Safety and control must be built into the computing architecture,” Jensen Huang said [1]. It is a company’s own claim; the test is an audit log, not a keynote.

nigeria-is-the-fifth-country.title: Nigeria is the fifth country, and the clock started on 11 October
nigeria-is-the-fifth-country.dek: Nigeria has confirmed its first case of Bundibugyo Ebola, a woman who travelled from Uganda. Nine days passed between her visit to a clinic in Abuja and a laboratory result. Those nine days are now the work.
nigeria-is-the-fifth-country.text: Nigeria has confirmed its first case of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus, the World Health Organization said on Wednesday [1]. The patient is a woman who had recently travelled from Uganda. She developed symptoms on 7 October, four days after arriving, sought care at a private health facility in Abuja on 11 October, and was confirmed by laboratory testing on 20 October [1]. She is in isolation and receiving care [1]. The nine days. Desk arithmetic: 11 October to 20 October is nine days between her first visit to a clinic and a confirmed result. That gap is where contacts accumulate. Nigerian authorities have so far identified 44 contacts under monitoring, and infection control is being strengthened at the clinic where she was seen [1]. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention has activated its incident management system, and WHO is supplying protective equipment and help with tracing [1]. The wider picture. Nigeria is the fifth country to detect the disease since the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was declared in mid-May [1]. The ECDC counts 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 deaths in the DRC, from data to 18 October [2]. There is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for this species [1]. WHO has not recommended any restrictions on travel or trade, and asks countries in the region to keep a high level of readiness [1]. For readers in Europe. The ECDC’s modelling still puts the risk of importation into the EU/EEA at very low, even in a pessimistic scenario, though sporadic imported cases cannot be excluded [2]. Nothing here is a reason to change your plans. The constructive reading: a new country is bad news, but a case found, isolated and surrounded by a list of 44 names is the system catching up. Watch the list, not the map.

kenyas-cases-came-from-the-quarantine-li.title: Kenya's cases came from the quarantine list
kenyas-cases-came-from-the-quarantine-li.dek: Kenya has eight confirmed Bundibugyo cases. Six of the seven after the first were people already in quarantine, according to the ECDC's timeline.
kenyas-cases-came-from-the-quarantine-li.text: Kenya had eight confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases, including one death, as of 20 October, the ECDC says [1]. The first was a Kenyan citizen living in the DRC who travelled home via Uganda on 3 October; the case was reported on 6 October, and the patient died [1]. Then the tracing shows up in the timeline. The second case, on 14 October, was a close family contact who was already in quarantine [1]. The third, on 16 October, was another close relative, also in quarantine [1]. On 17 October four more were confirmed: one relative and three health workers, all of whom had been in contact with the first case and had been placed in quarantine [1]. The eighth case, reported on 18 October, was a patient attendant, according to the health ministry’s director-general [1]. The ECDC does not say whether that person was on the list. Desk arithmetic: six of the seven cases after the first were found among people already in quarantine. That is what containment looks like from the inside: new cases, but on a list someone wrote in advance. UN News, citing WHO on Wednesday, gives nine Kenyan cases linked to the DRC [2]; the two counts are a day apart and may simply differ in timing.

an-appointment-should-not-ask-your-insur.title: An appointment should not ask your insurer
an-appointment-should-not-ask-your-insur.dek: Coalition politicians from the CSU and SPD want doctors' appointments given by medical need, not by public or private insurance, ahead of a primary-care reform due in November.
an-appointment-should-not-ask-your-insur.text: Health minister Carsten Linnemann plans to present a primary-care reform “probably in November”, with GP-first referrals and an appointment guarantee [1]. On Wednesday, CSU and SPD politicians said public or private insurance should no longer decide who gets a specialist slot first [1]. The statutory insurers’ federation called need-based booking “overdue”; the private insurers’ association said its members are about 10% of patients and cannot cause the waits of the other 90% [1]. Depending on the study, publicly insured patients wait 36 to 41 days on average [1]. Part of the fix may sit in the booking software: Holetschek suggested online portals stop asking [1].

the-curfew-moved-to-eleven.title: The curfew moved to eleven
the-curfew-moved-to-eleven.dek: Paris and Lyon renewed their night-time restrictions for Wednesday night, and Lyon's now starts two hours later. The justice minister counted 2,500 people taken into custody since the violence began. Attention shifts to Saturday.
the-curfew-moved-to-eleven.text: The Paris police prefecture has issued new orders for Wednesday night. They “prohibit the presence of adults as well as minors” in the République and Halles areas from 23:00 until 06:00 on Thursday [1]. In Lyon, the Rhône prefect renewed the curfew and the ban on gatherings, but it now starts at 23:00 instead of 21:00 [1]. That is the most useful line of the day: the authorities are giving back two hours of the evening because the previous nights were calm. The count. Justice minister Gérald Darmanin, visiting Marseille, said there had been 2,500 police custody cases since the violence began, and 174 people have been sent to prison for handling stolen goods or assault [1]. He said most of them had no criminal record [1]. Those are the numbers of a justice system working through a backlog, and they will keep rising for a while after the streets go quiet. Saturday. The weekend is the test. The yellow-vest coordination has filed a route for Saturday from Bastille to Opéra; the police prefecture had not confirmed it by Wednesday morning [1]. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez has sent instructions to prefects, including to ban gatherings “likely to disturb public order” [1]. In Toulon, the Var prefect banned face coverings in public from Wednesday 14:00 to Monday 09:00, set a Saturday curfew for unaccompanied minors and banned demonstrations in the city centre for that day [1]. Toulouse’s Ligue 1 match was moved from Saturday to Sunday at the prefecture’s request [1]. The tone at the top. Speaking from Doha, President Emmanuel Macron said a state of emergency was not needed and that the measures in place had brought calm back since Monday [1]. He will meet the intelligence services on Thursday morning for a detailed account of 17 October [1]. For you, if you live in or are travelling to a French city this week: the rules are set by local orders, street by street, and they change daily. Read the prefecture’s order for your area rather than a national headline.

the-bundeswehr-raised-its-own-threat-lev.title: The Bundeswehr raised its own threat level
the-bundeswehr-raised-its-own-threat-lev.dek: An internal assessment rates the risk of Russian sabotage against German forces at home as 'considerable' for the first time. The defence ministry confirmed the rating on Wednesday.
the-bundeswehr-raised-its-own-threat-lev.text: An internal security analysis seen by WDR and SZ rates the threat of Russian sabotage against the Bundeswehr as “erheblich” (considerable) for the first time, the second-highest level on its scale [1]. For the first time, the armed forces assume they themselves could be a target of Russian attacks inside Germany [1]. The trigger was a farmer’s chance find in mid-September: a crashed drone near the Wunstorf air base, carrying a can of high explosive [1]. It resembles the drone used in the failed attack at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August [1]. Technical analysis by the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) reportedly found the Wunstorf drone had lain there for about two years and may have been aimed at military aircraft [1]. The paper says the threat can no longer be limited to particular sites [1]. Russia has always denied involvement in sabotage [1]. At the government press conference on Wednesday, a defence ministry spokesman confirmed the “considerable” rating [2]. He gave examples of the response: more staff on guard and patrol, and extra technical protection such as infrared cameras and fence monitoring [2]. The reassuring part is the boring part: a written threat scale, a rating that moved, and fences that get cameras.

the-order-to-leave-riyadh.title: The order to leave Riyadh
the-order-to-leave-riyadh.dek: Late on Wednesday Washington moved from warning its people in Saudi Arabia to sending its non-emergency staff home. An ordered departure is an administrative act, and administrative acts are the ones worth reading.
the-order-to-leave-riyadh.text: The US State Department has ordered all non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, CBS News reported on Wednesday evening [1]. The spokesperson, Tommy Pigott, gave the reason in one line: the Houthis have “increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia”, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure [1]. The order follows Sunday’s round of embassy alerts in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE and several other countries, which warned that the fighting could spread without warning [1]. The same live page carries the quieter half of the evening. Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, shut on 10 October, saw a limited number of Saudia and flynas flights on Wednesday, while Lufthansa and Air France have cancelled flights through mid-November [1]. And the US Treasury sanctioned a Panamanian-Greek law firm and shipping agents in Singapore and the UAE over Iran’s “shadow fleet” of tankers [1]. A warning is a paragraph; an ordered departure is a list of names, seats and leases being closed. It tells you more about how a government reads the risk than any speech this week did. Nothing here is advice.

berlin-watches-the-31-october-marches.title: Berlin is watching the 31 October marches
berlin-watches-the-31-october-marches.dek: Asked whether large protests modelled on France could turn violent in Germany, the interior ministry separated peaceful school protests from an extremist scene.
berlin-watches-the-31-october-marches.text: Large demonstrations are announced in Germany for 31 October [1]. On Wednesday the interior ministry drew a line between peaceful school pupils’ protests and a violent extremist scene that may use them [1]. Federal and state agencies are sharing information, including with France and Italy, the ministry said [1]. The domestic intelligence service is watching relevant websites and social media; the federal police can help state police and turn back people at the border who intend to join violence [1]. It gave no estimate of numbers [1]. Peaceful protest is the default; policing should be built for that.

the-annex-the-point-of-return.title: The Annex: the point of return, read line by line
the-annex-the-point-of-return.dek: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, out today in Nairobi, says 1.5°C will be passed and sets out what it would take to come back below it. Read as a document, it is a ledger of required cuts against pledged ones, with a column of things that already worked.
the-annex-the-point-of-return.text: Today’s annex is the UN Environment Programme’s Emissions Gap Report 2026, “The Point of Return”, published in Nairobi on Wednesday and read here through UNEP’s own release [1]. What it assumes. That global warming will pass 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels [1]. The question it asks is narrower: what is the “lowest possible” overshoot? Its answer is a path on which warming peaks at 1.7–1.8°C around mid-century and returns to or below 1.5°C by 2100, with about a 50% chance [1]. What that path costs in emissions. Global greenhouse gas emissions would have to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, all against 2025 [1]. Full implementation of national pledges, the NDCs, would give 5–8% by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035 [1]. The required rate is 5.7% a year for 2025–2035, faster than the roughly 5% in the IPCC’s earlier pathways [1]. What happens without it. Current policies point to 2.8°C this century; delivered pledges to 2.6°C [1]. UNEP says both are worse than last year’s projections because of the United States’ withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and revised estimates of historical emissions [1]. Every five years of CO2 at current levels adds about 0.1°C to peak warming [1]. The column that already worked. More than 220 policy evaluations are cited. Electricity-sector policies cut emissions by an average of 9%; carbon taxes and cap-and-trade schemes by 5–13% [1]. Since the Paris Agreement, global renewable capacity has grown three times faster than anticipated and solar seven times faster [1]. If that continues, with additional policy, the world would be on track to triple renewable capacity by 2030 [1]. The caveat it states itself. The path also needs the removal and permanent storage of about 320 gigatonnes of CO2 this century, roughly eight years of 2024’s emissions, and UNEP calls the chances of achieving that “uncertain” [1]. The reading. Strip out the adjectives and the document is a set of rates, a gap between two columns, and a list of policies with measured effects. “Overshoot is not surrender,” said UN Secretary-General António Guterres [1]. The more useful sentence is the dull one: the tools that cut 9% in electricity are known, and the report counts them.

gard-left-orange-the-rivers-did-not-yet.title: Gard left orange; the rivers take longer
gard-left-orange-the-rivers-did-not-yet.dek: Météo-France lifted Gard's orange flood warning on Wednesday morning, the last one in France. The gauge record shows why the warning lasted after the rain.
gard-left-orange-the-rivers-did-not-yet.text: After Var and Alpes-Maritimes, Gard came out of orange on Wednesday, Météo-France announced in its latest bulletin; no département was left in orange [1]. The forecaster called it a Mediterranean episode “qui aura été remarquable” [1]. It caused flooding, closed roads, evacuations and power cuts, and two people died, in Saint-Mitre-les-Remparts in Bouches-du-Rhône and in Haute-Corse [1]. The daily gauge records explain the order in which warnings came down. At Nîmes-Courbessac, 134.3 mm fell in the 48 gauge days from 1 September to 18 October, then 151.6 mm in the single gauge day to 08:00 on 20 October [2]. Mont Aigoual recorded 191.5 mm in that day and Montpellier airport 111.7 mm [2]. Desk arithmetic: at Nîmes, one day brought more rain than the seven weeks before it. Water like that falls in hours and drains through a catchment over days. Rain warnings come down first; river warnings follow when the gauges allow. Wednesday’s map is the system completing that sequence, step by step.

the-rhine-gave-the-rain-back.title: The Rhine gave the rain back
the-rhine-gave-the-rain-back.dek: Kaub climbed to 21 cm early on Tuesday and is down to 11 cm again. The lowest low-water level on the station's record was 25 cm.
the-rhine-gave-the-rain-back.text: The Rhine gauge at Kaub read 11 cm at 16:15 on Wednesday, according to the federal waterways administration [1]. It had risen from 7 cm on Sunday afternoon to 21 cm early on Tuesday, then fell back through Wednesday [1]. The lowest low-water level in the station’s record was 25 cm, on 22 October 2018 [1]. Desk arithmetic: today’s reading is 14 cm below that. A gauge reading is measured from a fixed gauge zero, not from the riverbed, so it is not the depth of the shipping channel.

de-power-day-ahead.title: Wholesale power moved in autumn, not spring
de-power-day-ahead.subtitle: Germany/Luxembourg day-ahead electricity price, daily average, € per MWh
de-power-day-ahead.source: Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de, day-ahead price DE-LU (filter 4169) · CC BY 4.0
de-power-day-ahead.alt: Line chart of the daily average German-Luxembourg day-ahead electricity price since July 2025, in euros per megawatt hour. Monthly averages stay mostly between about €77 and €110 through July 2026, including the months after the war begins at the end of February; the daily low is −€16.34 on 5 April. The price climbs from August, averaging €144.82 in September with a daily high of €256.55 on 14 September, and €169.93 over 1 to 21 October, against €94.14 over the same days of 2025. The latest value, for delivery on 21 October 2026, is €211.94.

ea-hicp-dfr-21oct.title: The print the committee is looking at
ea-hicp-dfr-21oct.subtitle: HICP, annual change, % (core excludes energy, food, alcohol, tobacco) · ECB deposit rate, %, month-end
ea-hicp-dfr-21oct.source: Eurostat prc_hicp_minr (CC BY 4.0) · ECB Data Portal FM.D.U2.EUR.4F.KR.DFR.LEV
ea-hicp-dfr-21oct.alt: Line chart since January 2024 of euro-area HICP inflation, core inflation and the ECB deposit rate. Headline inflation is between 1.7% and 2.8% through 2024 and 2025, is 1.9% in February 2026, then rises after the energy shock to 3.8% in September 2026; core inflation stays between 2.2% and 2.6% through 2026 and is 2.5% in September. The deposit rate steps down from 4% to 2% by mid-2025 and back up to 2.5% by September 2026.

unep-gap-cuts-21oct.title: What is needed, and what is pledged
unep-gap-cuts-21oct.subtitle: Cut in global greenhouse gas emissions relative to 2025, %
unep-gap-cuts-21oct.source: UN Environment Programme, Emissions Gap Report 2026: The Point of Return (press release, Nairobi, 21 Oct 2026)
unep-gap-cuts-21oct.alt: Bar chart of cuts in global greenhouse gas emissions relative to 2025 in UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026. The lowest 1.5°C overshoot path needs 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040. Full implementation of national pledges (NDCs) gives 5–8% by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035; the bars show the upper ends, 8% and 15%.

2035 — needed for the lowest 1.5°C overshoot path
2040 — needed for the lowest 1.5°C overshoot path
